title: Deep learning finds comet C/2020 T2 in a single ZTF image
summary: The Tails EfficientDet model identified the extended object C/2020 T2 in one Zwicky Transient Facility Twilight Survey image on 2020 October 7. Follow-up orbital work confirmed it as a long-period comet. The study reports this as the first comet discovery assisted by deep learning; it also recovered a previously known comet, which is not counted as a new discovery here.
ai_technology: Tails, an EfficientDet-based deep-learning comet detector
organization: California Institute of Technology; IPAC; Zwicky Transient Facility collaboration

evidence.tested: The Tails EfficientDet model identified the extended object C/2020 T2 in one Zwicky Transient Facility Twilight Survey image on 2020 October 7.
evidence.unknown: The model surfaced the object, while human/standard follow-up established its orbit and comet classification. The entry counts only the newly discovered C/2020 T2, not recovery of P/2016 J3/P/2021 A3 or the detector’s performance metrics.
evidence.ai_role: Detected the comet’s extended coma/tail morphology in a single survey image and surfaced C/2020 T2 for discovery/follow-up; this enabled detection without requiring multi-epoch orbit linking at the initial search stage.
